sentences.text: This massive creature reached an estimated length of 15 meters and weighed approximately 20 tonnes.
Its middle and rear tail vertebrae feature a triangular pneumatic hole in the centrodiapophyseal fossa.
The rearmost neck vertebrae possess a small upward-pointing protuberance at the lower end of the postzygodiapophyseal lamina.
Additionally, the sacral vertebrae display boat-shaped joint facets on their centra.
The type specimen was discovered in Chubut Province, Argentina, near the Chubut River.
Local farmer Dionide Mesa reported the fossil in March 2001.
The generic name Bicharracosaurus combines the Spanish word for 'big animal' and the Greek word for 'lizard'.
The specific name dionidei honors the farmer who found the specimen.
Bicharracosaurus is classified as a macronarian sauropod, possibly related to brachiosaurids.
It belongs to the unranked family Macronaria.
The animal lived during the Late Jurassic, specifically the Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian stages.
This corresponds to a time between 161.5 and 149.2 million years ago.
Fossils are known from the Cañadón Calcáreo Formation in Argentina.
The phylogenetic position of Bicharracosaurus has been tested using datasets containing basal eusauropods and neosauropods.
It is debated whether Bicharracosaurus is closely related to Tehuelchesaurus benitezii, as phylogenetic analyses yield inconsistent results regarding their relationship.
The early evolution of macronarians is hindered by incongruent phylogenetic positions of related taxa depending on the dataset used.
